findings.claim: The plan does not say how `kmctl summary nudge` passes through the ADR 0026 hand-off, and the hand-off as written would hurt every tool call in a project whose pin differs from the copy on PATH. `hand_off` in src/kmctl/pin.py runs every verb except `briefing` through uvx online (`offline=False`), which builds the pinned copy when uv has not cached it. The PostToolUse hook fires on every Write, Edit, MultiEdit and Bash call, so in such a project each call would start uvx, and an uncached build can hit the 10 s hook timeout. Claude Code then kills the hook, so the build may never finish and the next call waits again. A user-scope install (settings_path supports the user's settings.json) also fires the hook in projects pinned to a release from before this ticket. That release has no `summary nudge` verb, so it prints a Typer usage error and exits 2. The shell guard keeps the exit at 0, but every call still pays the uvx cost. The plan's "exits 0 with {} on any failure" covers only the nudge's own code. It needs to say whether `summary nudge` gets the briefing's treatment (offline probe, quiet or run locally when the pin is not cached) or skips the hand-off, and r2 needs a quiet case for a project pinned to another release.

The plan now says summary nudge never goes through the hand-off and the copy on PATH runs it itself, and r2 has a pinned-project case where uvx is never called. That settles p1 for a copy on PATH from this release or later. The older-copy case is still open; see p2.

The plan says a copy on PATH older than this release has no summary nudge verb, so the hook's guard turns its usage error into {}. That is wrong for v0.7.0 and v0.8.0. Their main calls hand_off(sys.argv[1:]) before Typer parses, and every verb but briefing goes to uvx online. They never reach a usage error. When the project pins another release, which it must for the PostToolUse entry to be deployed there, they start uvx after every Write, Edit, MultiEdit and Bash call. That is p1 again, in the usual upgrade state: the project's pin moved ahead of the copy on PATH. An exemption written into this release's hand_off cannot reach copies that are already installed. The fix is small and needs no change to hand_off: the hook command sets KMCTL_PINNED=1 for the call (the CI action already does this, per ADR 0026). Every copy then runs the verb itself. A copy with the verb nudges, and an older one prints a usage error that the guard turns into {}. r2's missing-verb case should use a copy that has the hand-off (or a fake kmctl on PATH that would call uvx) and check that the hook command sets the variable. A copy that just lacks the verb does not test this.
The nudge no longer goes through the hand-off: the hook command sets KMCTL_PINNED=1, so the copy on PATH runs the verb itself and never starts uvx. r2 checks that a pinned project never calls uvx.

Copies v0.7.0 and v0.8.0 on PATH no longer hand off: with KMCTL_PINNED=1, their handoff_pin returns None before reading the lock, so main() falls through to app(), which gives a usage error (exit 2) on the missing verb. The hook's guard turns that into {}. r2 tests the missing-verb case with a fake kmctl.
